# The appointments Pazuzu made — and who is keeping them

The mistake is reading myths as entertainment. Pazuzu's cycle reads more like a charter — each story assigning a duty the modern world still pays for.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Pazuzu
- **Pantheon:** Mesopotamian
- **Domain of influence:** Wind Demon, Protection
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Technology & Innovation · Commerce & Governance · Society & Spirit
- **Strongest seat:** Wind & Atmospheric Energy
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 383 of 546

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Wind & Atmospheric Energy — through *Son of Ḫanbi, King of the Evil Wind-Demons*

Assyrian and Babylonian amulets introduce Pazuzu in the first person: 'I am Pazuzu, son of Ḫanbi, king of the evil lilû-demons. ' The formula identifies him as the head of a class of wind spirits and gives him a father, Ḫanbi, whose own name marks demonic ancestry.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Pazuzu is the demon of the west/southwest wind and king of the evil wind-demons; his canonical domain is the moving air that the turbine economy harvests.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Cybersecurity & Digital Protection — through *The Warden Against Lamashtu*

Lamashtu was the demoness who attacked pregnant women and newborns.  To stop her, families hung Pazuzu amulets and engraved plaques at doorways and bedsides.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *His apotropaic function — turning a powerful demon against other demons — maps onto threat detection, perimeter defense, and benign wards against malicious forces.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Disaster Resilience & Recovery — through *The Bronze Head from Assyria*

The most famous Pazuzu image is a bronze head in the Louvre (AO 19931), found in the region of ancient Assyria and dated to the 8th–7th century BCE.  It combines a leonine muzzle, bulging eyes, a scaly body, a serpent penis, scorpion tail, and eagle talons.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Pazuzu amulets were deployed against epidemic wind and child-killing demons; the figure is an ancient technology for mitigating invisible, airborne catastrophe.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services — through *The Southwest Wind in Mesopotamian Thought*

In Mesopotamian meteorology, certain winds were not weather but agents of disease.  The west and southwest winds could bring fever, crop-blight, and sand-storms.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Bronze heads and engraved plaques made Pazuzu a talismanic fixture of protective magic and later esoteric iconography.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Pazuzu has no long narrative epic; his 'mythology' is the archive of incantations, amulets, and bronze images that give him a precise job description. He is the demon you invoke when you need a worse demon driven off.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in wind & atmospheric energy, cybersecurity & digital protection, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/pazuzu/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
